assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Poly Medicure (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results. One reportable segment (medical devices), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the build (India + international organic + PendraCare/Citieffe + export incentives) sits in `revenueBuild` and POLYMED.ctx.js checks it reproduces model revenue. Revenue and EBITDA are on Screener's basis (FY26 ₹1,875 cr and ₹446 cr = 23.8%; the company's 'operating EBITDA' of ₹457.7 cr also includes the Egyptian associate's ₹5.7 cr, which Screener and we carry in other income, and excludes the ₹6.8 cr labour-code charge). Net Profit history is the attributable figure (POLYMED.patch.js); PendraCare's 10% minority (a share of losses) is carried in the tax line, so model EPS is EPS to Polymed's shareholders. No acquisitions beyond those closed by 30-Sep-2026. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS (the method of the brokers that disclose one: Waya 50x FY28E, IIFL 52x FY27 in Feb-2025, LKP ~50x FY27E, FundsIndia 61x FY26E; ICICI Securities used EV/EBITDA); EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Written by POLYMED.mult.js from `revenueBuild`. FY27E +22%: a full year of PendraCare and Citieffe (₹292 cr vs ₹117 cr for 4-6 months in FY26) plus organic growth of ~13% (Q1FY27 +12.4%); slightly below the ₹2,300-2,400 cr guidance because the Middle East (6-8% of revenue, −32% in Q1) is still blocked by shipping. FY28-29E +13-14%: India +16-17%, international organic +12.5-13% as new CE/FDA registrations, the two new plants and the recovery of West Asia come through; acquisitions +10% (Citieffe 10-12% in EUR guided; PendraCare flat until the Middle East recovers). Management's 'Vision 2030' (2x revenue by FY30, ~18% a year incl. ~20% acquired) needs more M&A than we assume.

revenueBuild._why: FY26 bases (Q4FY26 PPT; AR FY26 note 38): India ₹581.7 cr (+19.6%); international ₹1,280.2 cr, of which PendraCare ₹44.2 cr and Citieffe (Medistream group) ₹72.6 cr since acquisition, so international organic ₹1,163.5 cr (−0.6%); export incentives (other operating revenue) ₹13.3 cr. India +18 / 17 / 16% (FY26 +19.6%, Q1FY27 +16.2%, guidance '>20%' standalone; import substitution and hospital insurance); international organic +11.5 / 13 / 12.5% (Q1FY27 +10.4%: Europe +17.6% organic, RoW +4.0% with the Middle East −32%; guidance '>15%' standalone international); acquisitions ₹292 cr in FY27E (Q1FY27 ₹72.3 cr; FY26 pro-forma ₹260.5 cr = ₹116.7 cr + ₹104.9 cr + ₹38.9 cr), then +10% a year; export incentives ₹14 / 15 / 16 cr.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (excludes the associate). FY25 27.3%, FY26 23.8% (company 24.4% incl. associate; acquisitions and a weak export year), Q1FY27 23.8% with standalone at 28.0% helped by 4-5% price increases and inventory gains. Guidance: consolidated 23-25%, standalone 25-27% (upper end), subsidiaries 12-14% now, 18-20% in 2-3 years. FY27E 23.5%: standalone gross margin normalises to 68-69% (management), Haryana minimum wages +35% from Apr-2026, freight 2-3x, offset by price increases and H2 operating leverage. FY28E 23.8%: synergies at Citieffe/PendraCare and better export mix, less two new plants' start-up costs and R&D rising from 1.7% towards ~3% of sales. FY29E 24.3%. We do not assume a return to FY24-25's 26-27% while the acquired businesses run at low margins. Each 1pp of FY28E margin is ~₹26 cr of EBITDA (~₹1.9 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27E ₹215 cr: guidance ₹200-225 cr (FY26 ₹296 cr standalone, ₹308 cr consolidated); Palwal/Faridabad plant by Mar-2027 and Noida/YEIDA in Q1FY28. FY28-29E ₹240 / 260 cr: management's asset turn of 1.2-1.4x on new capacity implies ~₹230-270 cr a year for ₹300-350 cr of extra revenue; CRISIL expects ₹200-300 cr a year from internal accruals. Excludes acquisitions and the ₹33 cr Himalayan Mineral Water IBC payment (already paid in FY26).
assumptions._depWhy: Q1FY27 D&A ₹36.3 cr (₹145 cr annualised, incl. amortisation of ~₹131 cr of acquired intangibles); FY26 ₹116 cr. 5.8% of average gross block gives ₹150 / 163 / 177 cr in FY27-29E, i.e. the Q1 run-rate plus the two new plants. Gross block includes ₹274 cr of goodwill (not amortised), which the single rate absorbs.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's treasury is net of ₹354 cr of borrowings and leases, so treasury income is built on gross cash and investments in otherIncome instead (POLYMED.ctx.js).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 29, AR FY25 note 25; checked in POLYMED.ctx.js): (1) treasury income at 6.33% (FY26 return on mutual funds, AR FY26 key ratios; FY26 treasury income ₹64.0 cr = 6.19% of average gross cash) on average gross cash and investments on our path (engine net cash plus debtBuild): ₹54.8 / 60.2 / 69.7 cr; (2) share of profit of the Egyptian associate (Ultra for Medical Products, 30%; FY25 ₹5.2 cr, FY26 ₹5.7 cr, Q1FY27 ₹1.6 cr; Screener books it in other income) ₹6.3 / 6.9 / 7.6 cr; (3) recurring government grants and miscellaneous income ₹10 cr (FY24 ₹6.2 cr, FY25 ₹8.4 cr, FY26 ₹15.4 cr); (4) foreign-exchange gains at 2.27% of international organic revenue, the FY24-26 average (FY24 ₹15.7 cr = 1.63%, FY25 ₹21.6 cr = 1.85%, FY26 ₹38.6 cr = 3.32%): ₹29.4 / 33.2 / 37.4 cr. Exporters gain when the rupee drifts down while receivables are outstanding; a flat rupee would remove this part (~₹2.2-2.7 of EPS). Not forecast: provisions written back. FY26 ₹120.1 cr (treasury ₹64.0 cr, forex ₹38.6 cr, grants/misc ₹15.4 cr, other ₹2.0 cr); twelve months to Jun-26 ₹117 cr (Screener). FY27E is lower because the QIP cash was spent on PendraCare, Citieffe and capex (gross cash ₹1,227 cr at Mar-25, ₹842 cr at Mar-26).

debtBuild._why: Borrowings and leases ₹354 cr at Mar-26 on Screener (₹341.6 cr of debt: ~₹250 cr standalone revolving working-capital lines, Citieffe's ~€9 mn of loans repaid at €1.5-2 mn a year, PendraCare none; plus ₹12 cr of leases). We hold working-capital lines flat and repay ~₹15-20 cr a year: ₹340 / 320 / 300 cr. Interest at 7.3% of average debt (Q1FY27 ₹6.5 cr annualised on ~₹354 cr; FY26 ₹18.3 cr on a lower average).

assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on working-capital and acquisition debt and leases
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Built in `taxBuild` and written by POLYMED.mult.js.

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = (tax on PBT + minorities) / PBT. ₹ crore. Minorities are negative while PendraCare makes losses.
taxBuild._why: FY26 effective tax 25.0% (106.7/427.5), FY25 25.2%; Q1FY27 27.3% because subsidiary losses earn no tax credit. 26.0% / 25.5% / 25.2% as the acquired businesses move to profit. Minorities: 10% of PendraCare's result (FY26 loss before tax ₹14.1 cr in six months; Screener minority share −₹1 cr in FY26 and Q1FY27).

assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹3.50 a share (₹35.5 cr, 11% of profit); FY25 ₹3.0 (~9%). Cash is earmarked for capex and acquisitions ('strategic reserve'), so we assume no special payouts.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 0.95 x 6% = 12.2%. Net debt is negative (gross cash ₹842 cr vs ₹354 cr of debt), so WACC ≈ cost of equity; beta 0.95 for a mid-cap exporter with crude-linked costs, tender pricing and acquisition risk (above defensive consumer healthcare).
dcf._tgWhy: 6% nominal: medical consumables grow with procedures, ageing and insurance (India ~13% a year, world ~5%), but prices are tender-driven.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13% (FY29E) to 8% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 24%: Polymed's consolidated margin with the acquired businesses; the standalone 26-27% is offset by lower-margin subsidiaries and rising R&D.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 6% of revenue (FY27-29E 9%; FY23-26 15-21% during the build-out).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Middle East reopens, Europe keeps its 17% organic pace, US approvals turn into real orders, the anti-dumping duty lifts renal, and Citieffe/PendraCare reach mid-teens margins with production moved to India.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Exports stay weak (West Asia, US tariffs, Chinese competition), the acquired businesses keep losing money, crude-linked costs and wages squeeze margins back towards 22%, and working capital keeps absorbing cash.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Polymed: every broker note we could read that discloses a method uses P/E on forward EPS (Waya 50x FY28E, Dec-2025; IIFL 52x FY27 in Feb-2025 before its Feb-2026 downgrade; LKP ~50x FY27E; FundsIndia 61x FY26E) except ICICI Securities (30x FY26E EV/EBITDA, 2024). 48.5x Sep-28E EPS = Polymed's median one-year-forward P/E from 1-Apr-2021 to 30-Sep-2026 (every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 288 points; market value at each date over the next full year's profit to shareholders, so the Aug-2024 QIP shares count only from their allotment; FY26 before the ₹16.5 cr labour-code and acquisition costs), 44.9x, x 1.082 (thin-peer-set rule: listed med-tech names are too few or too new, so the nine-name pharma factor for names outside the set, +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +8.2%) = 48.6x, nearest half-turn 48.5x. No trough years. Bull 60.5x / bear 39x = 75th / 25th percentiles x the factor. Sensitivities (not used): reported profit 48.5x, Screener EPS on year-end shares 50.5x, from Apr-2022 46x, wider healthcare set 44x, Laxmi Dental's same-window move 26x. Checked in POLYMED.ctx.js; written by POLYMED.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Polymed's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Apr-2021 (EV = price x shares at the date + net debt at the latest March, with the ₹985 cr net QIP proceeds deducted from the 22-Aug-2024 allotment; EBITDA = next full fiscal year, Screener FY22-26 and our FY27-28E), 31.5x, x 1.075 (the pharma EV/EBITDA factor for names outside the set, +7.5%; reproduced +7.5%) = 34x, applied to Sep-28E EBITDA plus the engine's Sep-28E net cash. Bull 39x / bear 26x = 75th / 25th percentiles x the factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.2% (cost of equity ≈ WACC: net cash), terminal growth 6%; the tax rate includes PendraCare's small minority; plus the engine's net cash at Mar-27.

cover.headline: India's medical-consumables champion is paying for its next leg of growth: exports stalled, two acquisitions lose money and returns have halved; but at 41.8x FY28E earnings, below its own history, the price discounts much of it. On the street's P/E method we see {{dcf.upside|chg}}
cover.lead: Poly Medicure makes ~1.9 bn single-use devices a year (it is the world's third-largest IV cannula maker) and exports two-thirds of them. After a decade of 15-20% growth, FY26 stalled: organic revenue +5%, exports down outside two European acquisitions (PendraCare, Citieffe) that added ₹117 cr of revenue and a ₹14 cr loss, and EBITDA margin down from 27% to 24%. Q1FY27 was better (organic +12.4%, standalone margin 28%) and management kept FY27 guidance of ₹2,300-2,400 cr. We forecast EPS of ₹34.1 / 40.0 / 47.4 for FY27-29E. The brokers that disclose a method use **P/E**, and so do we: **48.5x Sep-28E EPS (₹43.7)**, i.e. Polymed's 44.9x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (market value at each date, so the 2024 QIP is handled) adjusted +8.2% for the healthcare re-rating, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,321; DCF ₹678. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Highly automated plants, EU MDR approvals on every site, ~68% standalone gross margin and 15-20-year distributor relationships make Polymed the low-cost, quality-approved supplier of IV cannulae, infusion sets and vascular-access devices to 125+ countries. India (31% of revenue) grows ~20% a year on import substitution.

Two QIPs (₹1,400 cr), ₹1,155 cr of capex in four years and ~₹390 cr for PendraCare and Citieffe have built capacity (65-70% used) and new segments (cardiology, orthopaedics, dialysis machines), but ROCE fell to 12%, free cash flow has been negative for four years and FY27E EPS grows only ~3% as D&A, interest and lower treasury income absorb the EBITDA gain.

arguments.h: Our numbers are below the bulls'
arguments.p: We keep consolidated margins near 24% (guidance 23-25%) rather than the ~28% older notes assumed, and include forex gains only at their three-year average. FY28E EPS ₹40.0 is ~11% below Waya's; EPS still compounds ~13% a year to FY29E as the acquisitions and new plants contribute.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price did the de-rating
arguments.p: The stock is down 46% from its Nov-2024 peak and trades at 41.8x FY28E vs a 44.9x median since 2021, while healthcare multiples re-rated. Our 48.5x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} (+27%): a BUY on our rule, with a wide range (bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}) and a DCF that says the price rests on the multiple.

sections.title: What Polymed does: makes ~1.9 bn low-cost disposable devices a year in India and sells two-thirds of them abroad; now adding dialysis, cardiology and orthopaedics

blocks.p: **Products.** Polymed makes single-use medical devices: **infusion therapy** (IV cannulae, where it is the world's third-largest maker with ~11% share and ~600 mn pieces a year, infusion sets, needle-free connectors, stopcocks, extension lines, prefilled saline syringes), **vascular access and critical care** (PICC lines, central venous catheters, implantable ports and midlines, much of it from Plan1Health in Italy), **renal care** (haemodialysers, blood lines, fistula needles, peritoneal dialysis sets and its own dialysis machine, ~1,100 installed), **transfusion** (blood bags, leukodepletion filters), and newer lines: **cardiology** (drug-eluting stents, balloons, drug-coated balloons, lithotripsy, plus PendraCare's guiding and diagnostic catheters) and **orthopaedics** (Citieffe's trauma implants and fixators). Most items sell for ₹10-20; the new lines sell for thousands of rupees.

**Customers.** About two-thirds of revenue is exported to 125+ countries, mainly through 1,000+ distributors and to other device makers (OEMs) that sell under their own brands; in India it sells to corporate and standalone hospitals and government tenders through distributors and 590+ own sales staff. **Factories:** 15 plants in five countries, heavily automated (400+ moulding machines, 530+ automatic assembly machines, 130+ robots) with in-house mould making and sterilisation. That cost base is the business: Polymed wins by making a quality-approved product (EU MDR, CE, some FDA) more cheaply than multinationals.

(1) The Aug-2024 QIP changed the share count (+5.5%) and added ₹985 cr of cash, so we compute the forward P/E on market value at each date rather than on today's share count. sections.title: Industry: a USD 680 bn global market growing ~5%, India only USD 16 bn but growing ~13%; disposables are competitive and tender-priced

blocks.p: Medical devices are a USD 650-680 bn global market growing ~5% a year, of which consumables and disposables are roughly a quarter; India is only ~2% of it (USD ~16 bn in 2025, per BCG/EY figures quoted by the company) but grows ~13% a year and imports 60-70% of what it uses. Polymed sells mostly low-cost, high-volume disposables (IV cannulae, infusion sets, blood bags, catheters) where scale, quality approvals and cost decide share, and is adding higher-value lines (dialysis, critical care, cardiology, orthopaedics) where clinical data and registrations take 2-3 years. About two-thirds of its sales are exports to 125+ countries, mainly to distributors and OEMs; the buyers are price-sensitive tenders and hospital groups, and the main rivals are multinationals (BD, B. Braun, Terumo, Nipro, Fresenius, Teleflex) and, increasingly, Chinese makers.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the India tailwind is real and Polymed captures it; it is why we model 16-18% domestic growth. The export tailwind that justified the 2024 rating ("China+1", the US) has not shown up in the numbers: organic exports were flat in FY26 and the US is still tiny. We model international organic growth of 11.5-13%, which needs the Middle East to reopen and the new CE/FDA registrations to sell.

sections.title: Infusion therapy and vascular access: half of revenue, a global cost leader, but it did not grow in FY26

blocks.p: Infusion therapy (₹997 cr, 53% of FY26 revenue) is the business Polymed was built on: IV cannulae (safety and standard), infusion sets, extension lines, stopcocks, needle-free connectors and, recently, prefilled saline syringes. Polymed says it is the world's third-largest IV cannula maker with ~11% of global volume (~600 mn pieces a year), and its 390+ patents are mostly safety features on these products. Vascular access and critical care (PICC lines, central venous catheters, ports, midlines, arterial catheters; much of it designed at Plan1Health in Italy) sits in "others" and is one of the faster-growing lines. **FY26 was flat:** infusion revenue fell 1.5% (restated basis) as European distributors worked down stock, US orders paused on tariffs and Middle-East shipments stopped. **Q1FY27: +11.1%**, with India infusion +20% (more value-added products and price increases) and exports recovering.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a good, cash-generative core with modest growth: we expect ~10-12% a year (India faster, exports slower). It is not a moat in the strict sense: the products are copied and the buyers are price-driven, but scale, approvals and cost give Polymed a durable edge over most Indian and Chinese rivals.

sections.title: Renal care: ₹188 cr and the only Indian dialyser maker, but Chinese imports set the price

blocks.p: Polymed was the first Indian company to make dialysis consumables (haemodialysers, blood lines, fistula needles, transducer protectors, peritoneal sets) and now sells its own dialysis machine (450 placed in FY26, ~1,100 installed by Jul-2026). Machines matter because each one pulls through a stream of consumables. Renal revenue grew from ₹26 cr (FY20) to ₹187.6 cr (FY26; +24.5%), but fell 3.8% in Q1FY27: Chinese makers ship dialysers into India duty-free from ASEAN plants, while Polymed pays duty on imported raw materials ("cost inversion"). Polymed chose to raise prices rather than defend volume and asked the government for protection: an anti-dumping investigation into dialysers from China and Malaysia has been opened, with a 20% injury margin claimed. Management still targets 15-20% growth in FY27 and hired a renal head from Nipro/Fresenius/DaVita.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** renal is the clearest example of Polymed's strategy and its limits. The installed base of machines is a real annuity, but the consumable is a commodity and the price is set by Chinese imports. An anti-dumping duty (a decision is possible within months, per management) would help; without it we would expect 10-15% growth, not 20%+. We do not model a duty.

sections.title: Cardiology and orthopaedics: ₹78 cr a quarter, mostly bought in 2025, loss-making so far; the "Polymed 3.0" bet

blocks.p: **Cardiology** (Q1FY27 ₹28.6 cr vs ₹2.9 cr) has two parts. Home-grown: drug-eluting stents (launched 2025; ~13,000 deployed by Jul-2026, still only ~₹10-12 cr of revenue a year), PTCA and drug-coated balloons and intravascular lithotripsy, backed by a 2,000-patient registry (PACIFIER, 840+ enrolled). Bought: **PendraCare** (Netherlands, 90% from 22-Sep-2025, EV €18.8 mn), which makes guiding and diagnostic catheters, partly for two large OEMs. Its CY25 revenue was €8.2 mn with EBITDA of just €84k, it lost ₹14.1 cr before tax in its first six months, and ~20% of its sales go to the Middle East, so it is not growing this year. **Orthopaedics** (Q1FY27 ₹49.2 cr) is **Citieffe** (Bologna; 100% from 6-Nov-2025, EV €31 mn): trauma implants, external fixators and a navigation system for nailing, sold directly in Italy, the US and Mexico (#2 in Italy and Mexico). CY25 revenue was flat at €17.7 mn (a LatAm tender was cancelled) with EBITDA of €3.15 mn (18%); management guides 10-12% growth in EUR for FY27 and plans to add plates (doubling its market).

sections.title: Exports and approvals: Europe is back, the Middle East is blocked and the US, the biggest prize, is still under USD 4 mn

blocks.p: Two-thirds of revenue is exported. **Europe** (₹597 cr in FY26, +7%; Q1FY27 ₹187 cr, +44% reported and +17.6% organic) recovered after a year of customer de-stocking, helped by new distributors in Northern Europe, the UK and Germany. **Rest of world** (₹683 cr; Q1FY27 +4.0% organic) is hurt by the West-Asia war: the Middle East is 6-8% of revenue and fell 32% in Q1FY27 because ships are not calling at Gulf ports, though orders are intact. **The US** is the opportunity Polymed keeps promising: Polymed has ~4 FDA 510(k) clearances of its own (3-4 more pending), Citieffe 10 (8-10 pending), PendraCare its guiding catheter; the group counts 15 approvals and 11-13 in the pipeline, has signed group-purchasing (GPO) contracts and hired a US sales head. But US exports will be only USD 3.5-4 mn in FY27 (<2% of revenue), a 10% tariff applies and management calls the policy "fluid".

sections.title: Capacity: 15 plants, 65-70% used, two more coming; the expansion shows up as depreciation, wages and working capital before it shows up as profit

blocks.p: Polymed has ~95,000 m² of plants and ~1.9 bn units a year of capacity (from ~1.0 bn and 63,000 m² in FY20), in Faridabad, Jaipur (two SEZ units) and Haridwar (two plants), plus Italy, the Netherlands, China and the Egyptian associate. Management says capacity built after the 2021 QIP is 65-70% used. Two more plants are under construction: **Palwal/Faridabad** (orthopaedics, transfusion and extra infusion capacity; online by Mar-2027) and **Noida/YEIDA medical-device park** (cardiology; commercial in Q1FY28). Capex was ₹239 / 277 / 331 / 308 cr in FY23-26; guidance is ₹200-225 cr for FY27. Management expects asset turns of 1.2-1.4x on new capacity.

blocks.callout: **Verdict: a narrow edge, not a wide moat.** Polymed's advantages (scale, automation, approvals, long distributor relationships) are real and have produced a decade of 15-20% growth at ~25% EBITDA margins, better than any listed Indian peer. But they protect a commodity-like product line against other low-cost makers only partly (renal shows what Chinese pricing can do), and in the new segments (cardiology, orthopaedics, the US) Polymed is a small, late entrant against entrenched multinationals and Indian specialists such as Meril. The premium valuation assumes the new segments succeed.

sections.title: Revenue ×3 since FY19 and EPS ×4.5 to FY25, then a stall: FY26 organic growth was 5%, margins fell 3pp and EPS slipped

blocks.p: Polymed's revenue grew from ₹610 cr in FY19 to ₹1,875 cr in FY26 (17% a year) in three phases. **FY19-21: bootstrapped.** Growth of 13-18% a year funded from its own cash; EBITDA margin rose to 28% in FY21 on COVID-era demand for infusion and critical-care consumables. **FY22-25: the QIP-funded build-out.** Two share sales (₹400 cr in 2020, ₹1,000 cr in Aug-2024) paid for capacity, renal and new segments; revenue grew 17-23% a year and EPS rose from ₹15.3 to ₹33.4. **FY26: the stall.** Exports fell 3-4% outside the acquisitions (European customers' over-stocking, US tariffs, West-Asia shipping), so organic revenue grew only 5%; PendraCare and Citieffe added ₹117 cr of revenue but lost money; consolidated EBITDA margin fell from 27.3% to 23.8% (Screener) and EPS from ₹33.4 to ₹31.8 (₹33.0 before ₹16.5 cr of labour-code and deal costs).

sections.title: Capital allocation: ₹1,400 cr raised from shareholders, ₹1,155 cr of capex and ₹390 cr of acquisitions in four years; returns on capital have halved

blocks.p: Polymed has turned from a self-funded company into a capital-hungry one. It raised ₹400 cr in a QIP in Sep-2020 and ₹1,000 cr in Aug-2024 (53.2 lakh shares at ₹1,880, +5.5% to the share count). In FY23-26 it spent ₹1,155 cr on capex (new plants at Haridwar and Faridabad, Jaipur SEZ, gamma sterilisation, the Noida medical park) and ~₹390 cr in cash on PendraCare and Citieffe, against ₹936 cr of operating cash flow; free cash flow was negative in every one of those years on Screener's numbers. The result: capacity ahead of demand (65-70% used), a bigger product range and a balance sheet that is still net cash, but Screener's ROCE fell from 24% (FY24) to 12% (FY26) and ROE to ~11%, below a ~12% cost of equity. The company prefers its own ROIC (21.4% standalone in FY26), which leaves out the cash, unused assets and the subsidiaries.

blocks.callout: **The acquisition arithmetic.** Polymed paid ~₹390 cr of cash (plus ~₹39 cr contingent and ₹81 cr of assumed debt) for two businesses with ~₹260 cr of revenue and almost no profit. Management says they can earn 12-14% EBITDA now and 18-20% in 2-3 years with Indian sourcing and production; on ₹290 cr that would be ₹35-58 cr of EBITDA, against ~₹25 cr a year of post-tax treasury income given up. The Plan1Health record says it can work; FY26 says it will take time.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts and a new auditor, but profit has not turned into free cash for four years, and a fifth of pre-tax profit is other income

bullets: **Other income is large:** ₹120 cr in FY26 (28% of PBT): treasury income on the QIP cash ₹64.0 cr (mostly mutual-fund gains, realised ₹40.2 cr and unrealised ₹12.6 cr), forex gains ₹38.6 cr, grants and miscellaneous ₹15.4 cr. Screener labels the mutual-fund gains "exceptional"; they are not, but they shrink as the cash is spent and swing with bond markets.
**One-offs in FY26:** a ₹6.8 cr labour-code provision and ₹9.7 cr of acquisition costs (₹12.4 cr after tax). Our base EPS is ₹33.0 vs ₹31.8 reported. No exceptional items in FY21-25.

**Cash conversion:** cash from operations before tax was 71-102% of EBITDA in FY15-26 (Screener), 78% in FY26; working capital absorbed ₹146 cr in FY26 (receivables ₹99 cr). Free cash flow (Screener) was negative in FY23-26: capex and working capital have outrun profit.

**Acquisition accounting:** PendraCare and Citieffe purchase-price allocations are provisional (AR FY26 note 38); ₹224 cr of goodwill and ~₹131 cr of intangibles were recognised, and contingent consideration (~₹39 cr) is a liability that can be revalued through profit.
**Pay is profit-linked:** promoter directors' commissions (₹11.2 cr each to the MD and JMD in FY26) rise with profit, a small but real cost to minorities.
**Audit:** Doogar & Associates since the Sep-2024 AGM (replacing the previous auditor); we found no qualification in the FY26 report.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing looks wrong, but three things deserve attention: heavy other income that will decline, four years of negative free cash flow, and provisional acquisition accounting. We value on EPS before the FY26 one-offs and include forex gains at their three-year average, which is the least certain part of our forecast.

sections.title: Balance sheet: still net cash (₹489 cr), but the QIP pile has shrunk by a third and working capital now ties up 44% of sales

blocks.p: At Mar-26 Polymed held ₹842 cr of cash, deposits and mutual funds (₹1,227 cr a year earlier) against ₹341.6 cr of borrowings (₹289.5 cr short-term working-capital lines, ₹52.1 cr long-term, mostly Citieffe's) and ₹12.0 cr of leases: net cash of ₹489 cr, ~3% of the market value. Cash was ₹854.7 cr at Jun-26. The weak spot is working capital: standalone receivables rose to 98 days (78) as Polymed gave export customers longer terms, inventory is ~150 days (2.5-3 months of raw material is kept deliberately), and suppliers are paid in ~35 days, so the standalone cash conversion cycle is 215 days (183). Consolidated, Screener's working-capital items are ~44% of sales, and every ₹100 cr of extra revenue needs ~₹44 cr of cash. Other items: goodwill ₹274 cr and acquired intangibles ~₹131 cr (16% of net worth together), a 10% minority in PendraCare (₹43 cr), ~₹39 cr of contingent deal payments, and ₹33 cr paid for Himalayan Mineral Water (IBC). CRISIL raised the outlook to AA-/Positive in Jun-2026.

sections.title: Valuation: 48.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, {{dcf.upside|chg}} from the 30-Sep close: BUY

blocks.p: Every broker note we could read that discloses a method values Polymed on **P/E** on forward EPS: Waya 50x FY28E (Dec-2025), IIFL 52x FY27 (Feb-2025, before its Feb-2026 downgrade), LKP ~50x FY27E (Mar-2025) and FundsIndia 61x FY26E (Dec-2024); only ICICI Securities used EV/EBITDA (30x FY26E, 2024). We follow the majority: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, on consolidated EPS to shareholders. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks.

The house rule (PLAYBOOK §4) starts from the stock's own one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, leaving out trough years, and multiplies the median by the sector's move against its own history. Four choices matter here. **(1) The Aug-2024 QIP.** Shares rose 5.5% on 22-Aug-2024 and ₹985 cr of cash came in. To keep per-share figures consistent with the share count at each date, we compute each point as market value on that date (price x shares outstanding then) ÷ the next full year's profit to shareholders; Screener-style EPS on year-end shares (46.8x) is a sensitivity. **(2) One-offs.** FY26 profit carries ₹16.5 cr of labour-code and acquisition costs (₹12.4 cr after tax, 4% of profit); the base uses profit before them (forecasts carry none) and the reported median (45.0x) is a sensitivity. **(3) Every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close** (288 points). **(4) The sector factor.** Listed Indian medical-device makers are too few or too new for a five-year median, so under the thin-peer-set rule we use the nine-name pharma factor for names outside the set: **+8.2%**. No own de-rating, growth or returns adjustment enters the base.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a world-class disposables maker in an expensive transition; at 41.8x FY28E the price already discounts a lot of disappointment: BUY

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest exporter of medical consumables: low-cost, highly automated plants, EU MDR approvals, 15-20-year distributor relationships, India growing ~20% a year on import substitution, and optionality in renal, cardiology, orthopaedics and the US. **What you are not buying:** pricing power, a proven US business, profitable acquisitions (yet) or free cash flow (negative for four years).

**What you are paying:** ₹1,674 is 53.8x trailing EPS, 49.1x our FY27E and 41.8x our FY28E EPS, against a 44.9x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021. Polymed's own trailing P/E is −12% vs its five-year median while the pharma set is +8.2%. On the street's method (P/E) and our derived 48.5x, the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a BUY. assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Poly Medicure (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results. One reportable segment (medical devices), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the build (India + international organic + PendraCare/Citieffe + export incentives) sits in `revenueBuild` and POLYMED.ctx.js checks it reproduces model revenue. Revenue and EBITDA are on Screener's basis (FY26 ₹1,875 cr and ₹446 cr = 23.8%; the company's 'operating EBITDA' of ₹457.7 cr also includes the Egyptian associate's ₹5.7 cr, which Screener and we carry in other income, and excludes the ₹6.8 cr labour-code charge). Net Profit history is the attributable figure (POLYMED.patch.js); PendraCare's 10% minority (a share of losses) is carried in the tax line, so model EPS is EPS to Polymed's shareholders. No acquisitions beyond those closed by 30-Sep-2026. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS (the method of the brokers that disclose one: Waya 50x FY28E, IIFL 52x FY27 in Feb-2025, LKP ~50x FY27E, FundsIndia 61x FY26E; ICICI Securities used EV/EBITDA); EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Written by POLYMED.mult.js from `revenueBuild`. FY27E +22%: a full year of PendraCare and Citieffe (₹292 cr vs ₹117 cr for 4-6 months in FY26) plus organic growth of ~13% (Q1FY27 +12.4%); slightly below the ₹2,300-2,400 cr guidance because the Middle East (6-8% of revenue, −32% in Q1) is still blocked by shipping. FY28-29E +13-14%: India +16-17%, international organic +12.5-13% as new CE/FDA registrations, the two new plants and the recovery of West Asia come through; acquisitions +10% (Citieffe 10-12% in EUR guided; PendraCare flat until the Middle East recovers). Management's 'Vision 2030' (2x revenue by FY30, ~18% a year incl. ~20% acquired) needs more M&A than we assume.

revenueBuild._why: FY26 bases (Q4FY26 PPT; AR FY26 note 38): India ₹581.7 cr (+19.6%); international ₹1,280.2 cr, of which PendraCare ₹44.2 cr and Citieffe (Medistream group) ₹72.6 cr since acquisition, so international organic ₹1,163.5 cr (−0.6%); export incentives (other operating revenue) ₹13.3 cr. India +18 / 17 / 16% (FY26 +19.6%, Q1FY27 +16.2%, guidance '>20%' standalone; import substitution and hospital insurance); international organic +11.5 / 13 / 12.5% (Q1FY27 +10.4%: Europe +17.6% organic, RoW +4.0% with the Middle East −32%; guidance '>15%' standalone international); acquisitions ₹292 cr in FY27E (Q1FY27 ₹72.3 cr; FY26 pro-forma ₹260.5 cr = ₹116.7 cr + ₹104.9 cr + ₹38.9 cr), then +10% a year; export incentives ₹14 / 15 / 16 cr.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (excludes the associate). FY25 27.3%, FY26 23.8% (company 24.4% incl. associate; acquisitions and a weak export year), Q1FY27 23.8% with standalone at 28.0% helped by 4-5% price increases and inventory gains. Guidance: consolidated 23-25%, standalone 25-27% (upper end), subsidiaries 12-14% now, 18-20% in 2-3 years. FY27E 23.5%: standalone gross margin normalises to 68-69% (management), Haryana minimum wages +35% from Apr-2026, freight 2-3x, offset by price increases and H2 operating leverage. FY28E 23.8%: synergies at Citieffe/PendraCare and better export mix, less two new plants' start-up costs and R&D rising from 1.7% towards ~3% of sales. FY29E 24.3%. We do not assume a return to FY24-25's 26-27% while the acquired businesses run at low margins. Each 1pp of FY28E margin is ~₹26 cr of EBITDA (~₹1.9 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27E ₹215 cr: guidance ₹200-225 cr (FY26 ₹296 cr standalone, ₹308 cr consolidated); Palwal/Faridabad plant by Mar-2027 and Noida/YEIDA in Q1FY28. FY28-29E ₹240 / 260 cr: management's asset turn of 1.2-1.4x on new capacity implies ~₹230-270 cr a year for ₹300-350 cr of extra revenue; CRISIL expects ₹200-300 cr a year from internal accruals. Excludes acquisitions and the ₹33 cr Himalayan Mineral Water IBC payment (already paid in FY26).
assumptions._depWhy: Q1FY27 D&A ₹36.3 cr (₹145 cr annualised, incl. amortisation of ~₹131 cr of acquired intangibles); FY26 ₹116 cr. 5.8% of average gross block gives ₹150 / 163 / 177 cr in FY27-29E, i.e. the Q1 run-rate plus the two new plants. Gross block includes ₹274 cr of goodwill (not amortised), which the single rate absorbs.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's treasury is net of ₹354 cr of borrowings and leases, so treasury income is built on gross cash and investments in otherIncome instead (POLYMED.ctx.js).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 29, AR FY25 note 25; checked in POLYMED.ctx.js): (1) treasury income at 6.33% (FY26 return on mutual funds, AR FY26 key ratios; FY26 treasury income ₹64.0 cr = 6.19% of average gross cash) on average gross cash and investments on our path (engine net cash plus debtBuild): ₹54.8 / 60.2 / 69.7 cr; (2) share of profit of the Egyptian associate (Ultra for Medical Products, 30%; FY25 ₹5.2 cr, FY26 ₹5.7 cr, Q1FY27 ₹1.6 cr; Screener books it in other income) ₹6.3 / 6.9 / 7.6 cr; (3) recurring government grants and miscellaneous income ₹10 cr (FY24 ₹6.2 cr, FY25 ₹8.4 cr, FY26 ₹15.4 cr); (4) foreign-exchange gains at 2.27% of international organic revenue, the FY24-26 average (FY24 ₹15.7 cr = 1.63%, FY25 ₹21.6 cr = 1.85%, FY26 ₹38.6 cr = 3.32%): ₹29.4 / 33.2 / 37.4 cr. Exporters gain when the rupee drifts down while receivables are outstanding; a flat rupee would remove this part (~₹2.2-2.7 of EPS). Not forecast: provisions written back. FY26 ₹120.1 cr (treasury ₹64.0 cr, forex ₹38.6 cr, grants/misc ₹15.4 cr, other ₹2.0 cr); twelve months to Jun-26 ₹117 cr (Screener). FY27E is lower because the QIP cash was spent on PendraCare, Citieffe and capex (gross cash ₹1,227 cr at Mar-25, ₹842 cr at Mar-26).

debtBuild._why: Borrowings and leases ₹354 cr at Mar-26 on Screener (₹341.6 cr of debt: ~₹250 cr standalone revolving working-capital lines, Citieffe's ~€9 mn of loans repaid at €1.5-2 mn a year, PendraCare none; plus ₹12 cr of leases). We hold working-capital lines flat and repay ~₹15-20 cr a year: ₹340 / 320 / 300 cr. Interest at 7.3% of average debt (Q1FY27 ₹6.5 cr annualised on ~₹354 cr; FY26 ₹18.3 cr on a lower average).

assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on working-capital and acquisition debt and leases
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Built in `taxBuild` and written by POLYMED.mult.js.

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = (tax on PBT + minorities) / PBT. ₹ crore. Minorities are negative while PendraCare makes losses.
taxBuild._why: FY26 effective tax 25.0% (106.7/427.5), FY25 25.2%; Q1FY27 27.3% because subsidiary losses earn no tax credit. 26.0% / 25.5% / 25.2% as the acquired businesses move to profit. Minorities: 10% of PendraCare's result (FY26 loss before tax ₹14.1 cr in six months; Screener minority share −₹1 cr in FY26 and Q1FY27).

assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹3.50 a share (₹35.5 cr, 11% of profit); FY25 ₹3.0 (~9%). Cash is earmarked for capex and acquisitions ('strategic reserve'), so we assume no special payouts.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 0.95 x 6% = 12.2%. Net debt is negative (gross cash ₹842 cr vs ₹354 cr of debt), so WACC ≈ cost of equity; beta 0.95 for a mid-cap exporter with crude-linked costs, tender pricing and acquisition risk (above defensive consumer healthcare).
dcf._tgWhy: 6% nominal: medical consumables grow with procedures, ageing and insurance (India ~13% a year, world ~5%), but prices are tender-driven.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13% (FY29E) to 8% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 24%: Polymed's consolidated margin with the acquired businesses; the standalone 26-27% is offset by lower-margin subsidiaries and rising R&D.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 6% of revenue (FY27-29E 9%; FY23-26 15-21% during the build-out).
